script.text: One inflation number just hit U.S. stocks hard. Could interest rates go up?
September consumer prices rose 3.7 percent from a year earlier, CNBC reports. Economists polled by Dow Jones expected 3.6. August was 3.4. Gasoline prices rose 9.1 percent, according to Mitrade.

Hotter inflation raises the odds that the Federal Reserve lifts rates again. CME FedWatch put an October hike near 39 percent, up from about 22 before the data. The ten year Treasury yield briefly topped 5.3 percent.
On Wednesday the S and P 500 closed down 1.11 percent at 7,718.94, Xinhua reports. It was the first drop of 1 percent in over 50 trading days. The Nasdaq lost 1.88 percent. The Dow slipped 0.09.
Will the Fed raise interest rates in October? Yes or no?

upload.description:
U.S. consumer prices rose 3.7% in September from a year earlier, above the 3.6% economists polled by Dow Jones expected, CNBC reports. The S&P 500 closed down 1.11% at 7,718.94 on Wednesday, its first 1% drop in over 50 trading days, Xinhua reports; the Nasdaq fell 1.88%. CME FedWatch put the odds of an October Fed rate hike near 39%.

Sources: CNBC, Xinhua, Mitrade, Seeking Alpha, Schwab (Oct 14, 2026).
